title: As a developer, I can rely on GPU-accelerated rendering that stays fast and responsive under heavy output
As a power-user, I can see published benchmarks or measured latency/throughput numbers backing the terminal's performance claims
As a developer, I can split windows into panes and organize work across tabs without an external multiplexer
As a developer, I can restore my windows, tabs, and working directories after a restart or crash
As a power-user, I can summon the terminal instantly with a global hotkey or quake-style dropdown window
As a developer, I can search my scrollback quickly and jump between matches
As a developer, I can open URLs and file paths from output by clicking them or selecting them from the keyboard
As a power-user, I can discover and run terminal actions from a searchable command palette
As a power-user, I can keep the terminal's full configuration as plain-text files in my dotfiles and sync it across machines
As a power-user, I can apply color schemes and themes, including automatic light/dark mode switching
As a developer, I can use programming fonts with ligatures, fallback fonts, and fine-grained font tuning
As a developer, I can jump between prompts and command marks in my scrollback thanks to shell integration
As a developer, I get command-aware features from shell integration, like exit status, duration, and notifications when long commands finish
As a developer, I can SSH to remote hosts with the terminal's own integration carrying my terminfo, shell integration, and config along
As a developer, I can use tmux inside the terminal, or a documented native tmux integration/control mode
As a developer, I can display inline images and rich graphics via a documented terminal graphics protocol
As a developer, I can run the same terminal with the same config on macOS, Linux, and Windows
As a developer, I can script and control the terminal from the command line — open windows, send text, query state — via a documented CLI or IPC interface
As an AI-native user, I can let a coding agent programmatically drive the terminal itself — create panes, run commands, read output — through a documented control protocol or API
As a power-user, I can define startup sessions and window layouts in config or scripts so a project workspace opens in one command
As a developer, I can extend the terminal with scripts or plugins in a real language (Lua, Python, kittens) beyond built-in options
As an AI-native user, I can delegate terminal tasks to a built-in AI agent that plans and executes commands with my approval
As an AI-native user, I can type natural language and get the right shell command generated in place
As an AI-native user, I can get AI explanations and suggested fixes when a command fails
As an AI-native user, I can use or fully disable AI features with clear control over what session data leaves my machine, without a forced login
